notes: §1985:IX.2.8.3 GR1: "The RERUN clause for the Indexed I-O module is a subset of the RERUN clause for the Sequential I-O module. Thus the specifications for the RERUN clause are located on page VII-17." One grammar rule (rerunClause) and one screen (ScreenRerunClauses, called by BindIoControl for every I-O-CONTROL paragraph whatever its files' organization) carry the Sequential module's clause, so the indexed subset gets the same specifications: the subset's two differences from the full format, a required ON phrase and no END OF REEL/UNIT phrase, fall out of §1985:VII.2.12.3 SR3 and SR2 for an indexed file-name-2, and SR1 refuses an indexed file-name-1. The 1985 arm is VisitRerunClause, which accepts the clause at --std 85 and refuses it from 2002 (COBOL0902); its integer-1 RECORDS phrase with an implementor-name records rerun points on the indexed file (§1985:VII.2.12.4 GR2 d, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.11). Probed at 85 on an indexed file: ON implementor-name with integer-1 RECORDS OF the file and with integer-2 CLOCK-UNITS compile and run; ON naming the indexed file (COBOL6529, COBOL6530), END OF REEL OF the indexed file (COBOL6529), RECORDS with no ON phrase (COBOL6530) and an undefined condition-name-1 (COBOL1639) are refused. The witness runs ON implementor-name EVERY 100 RECORDS OF an indexed file.

[ [ apply-commit-clause] . ] [ [ { same-clause }… ]. ] (no RERUN clause)". The 2023 I-O-CONTROL format allows only APPLY COMMIT and SAME clauses. RERUN is gone, so the 1985 rule on the Indexed I-O RERUN clause has no counterpart.
